key_insight: A dilated causal CNN can detect radiation-induced charge jumps in superconducting qubits fast enough for real-time, in-loop control.
engineering_relevance: The model was compiled to FPGA firmware on the QICK/ZCU216 platform, showing that low-latency, hardware-ready inference can replace offline charge-jump detection in quantum control systems.
method: Trained a dilated causal convolutional neural network on synthetic Ramsey tomography scans built from NEXUS-measured qubit templates.
Converted the network to FPGA firmware with hls4ml using ap_fixed<16,6> quantization.
Deployed for online inference on the Zynq UltraScale+ RFSoC with 6.19 μs latency per inference.
evidence_signal: At matched false-positive rate, the DCCNN achieved detection efficiency comparable to the offline χ² method (0.843 ± 0.022 vs. 0.866 ± 0.020) for |Δq| in [0.1, 0.5] e.
watch_item: Performance depends on synthetic training data and fixed-point FPGA quantization, so robustness to unseen experimental conditions and deployment drift should be validated.
paper_title: Real-Time Detection of Charge Jumps in Superconducting Qubits with a Convolutional Neural Network
